observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: The derived ABI record DETERMINES __thiscall; it no longer abstains. reconstruction/evidence/00b1fbf0/evidence.json, category abi_derived, carries verdict ABI_INFERRED with conflicts [] and states conventions.calling_convention __thiscall, conventions.confidence INFERRED, conventions.candidate_conventions ["__thiscall", "__fastcall"] and conventions.ambiguities []. The naming rule is V1-VFT and it is the only one of the record's six inferences (C5, R2, V1-VFT, S2, RT1, RT2) that carries a calling-convention claim; its text reads, verbatim: 'calling convention is __thiscall: 0x00b1fbf0 is slot 3 of the vptr-backed vftable at 0x013f57f8, so it is a virtual member of some class; the callee pops nothing and no stack word is read as an argument, so the receiver is in a register, and ECX is the only one that carries one', with value {cleanup_side caller, membership_count 443, receiver_provenance vftable_slot, receiver_register ECX, slot_index 3, table 0x013f57f8}. The previous record in this file, which asserted no convention on the strength of an ABI_UNKNOWN abstention, is superseded and was false. The wider claim the old observation made -- that the body is byte-identical under every convention -- remains true and is not what changed: the conventions differ only in what the CALLER puts in registers and pops, and this body consumes none of it. What changed is that the PORT is now determined, by rule, and NOT __fastcall: the record keeps __fastcall as a second surviving candidate and nothing observed here closes it.
observed_original_abi.return_observation: 0x00b1fbf0: MOV AL,0x1 writes only the low byte of EAX, so bits 8..31 of EAX are left as the caller left them rather than zeroed. Every consumer inspected tests the AL byte and never the full dword, and 0x00e81139 goes further and compares it against the immediate 1 (CMP AL,0x1), which is what makes the one-byte width falsifiable rather than decorative. The derived return record names register EAX and register_class integral and names NO width and NO type; the one-byte width here is established from the opcode (B0 is MOV r8,imm8, whose register field is fixed at AL), not copied from a record. The source return_type std::uint8_t is this project's own spelling of that fact.
observed_original_abi.hidden_this_register: ECX is the register V1-VFT names as carrying the receiver, and 0x00b1fbf0 never reads it: the two instructions mention no register other than AL. The port therefore carries a receiver the body discards.
observed_original_abi.receiver_observation: Two different records are in play and both are carried. The derived record's receiver sub-record has register ECX, provenance vftable_slot, confidence OBSERVED, present FALSE, bounds_only true, shape null, distinct_offsets 0, offsets [], max_offset null and written_through 0. `present: false` is rule R2, whose text reads 'ECX is never read in any form, so there is no register receiver'. That is an observation about the BODY and it does not contradict V1-VFT, which determines the PORT: the entry is reached as a __thiscall member with a receiver in ECX, and the body then ignores that register. The honest statement is 'entered as a __thiscall member whose body never reads its receiver', and the two halves are stated separately here rather than collapsed into a single receiver: true or false. Six direct call sites are corroboration for the port and are recorded in observed_mechanics and in corroborating_call_sites below; none of them is evidence that the body reads anything.
observed_original_abi.stack_cleanup_observation: stack_cleanup_bytes 0 and stack_cleanup_owner caller are INFERRED, not OBSERVED, and the derived record says so: cleanup.confidence INFERRED, cleanup.evidence 'ret with no immediate, no stack reads'. A bare RET with no immediate is compatible with caller cleanup and is also what a callee-side convention with nothing to pop would look like; the body consumes no stack word that could discriminate the two.

body_reconstruction.form: naked __thiscall transcription of the three observed bytes
body_reconstruction.claim_scope: The three-byte body is reconstructed byte for byte and the PORT is reconstructed as a __thiscall member. No semantic name, no owning class, no table identity, no receiver type and NO FIELD OFFSET in either direction are claimed.
body_reconstruction.form_rationale: Naked, because for a three-byte body a C++ restatement would be a second claim rather than a first one. Every compiler here emits the same two instructions from the same source, but g++ emits `mov eax,1` (B8 01 00 00 00) where the original and clang++ emit `mov al,1` (B0 01) -- a DIFFERENT machine body, one that writes all four bytes of the return register where the original writes one. The distinction is observable, and the model test measures it directly by reading the full EAX back after a call made with a poison pattern in its upper 24 bits.
preserved_semantics: the answer is the byte 0x01, not the dword 0x00000001: only AL is written and bits 8..31 of EAX are left as the caller left them
the receiver is never read, so any receiver including null and any unmapped address is accepted
no callee, no global and no memory access of any kind
a bare RET with no immediate, so the caller owns all stack cleanup and the callee pops zero bytes
the entry is a __thiscall member: the receiver arrives in ECX, which is what V1-VFT determined and what six call sites corroborate
body_reconstruction.byte_exactness: The emitted body is B0 01 C3, identical to the three bytes read live at 0x00b1fbf0, at every optimisation level under both compilers. The one toolchain artifact recognised and excluded is a ten-byte get_pc_thunk PC anchor (E8 rel32 then opcode 05) that g++ -m32 -O0 prepends to a naked function and clang++ never emits; it is recognised by that exact opcode pair and the three target bytes are then required immediately after it.

semantic_findings: The whole observable contract is 'return the byte 0x01'. There is no input, no state read and no side effect, so the function is a constant.

The PORT is now determined rather than modelled: rule V1-VFT names __thiscall from this address's membership in a vptr-backed vftable, and six call sites are read straight out of the image to show a concrete non-null value in ECX at the transfer. The previous revision of this record asserted no convention on the strength of an ABI_UNKNOWN abstention, and that assertion is superseded.

The determination is about the PORT, not the BODY, and the two must not be collapsed. The body never reads ECX -- rule R2, OBSERVED -- so `receiver.present` is false in the derived record while the entry is still a __thiscall member. Both halves are stated separately.

The same address is stored at four distinct slot offsets across three distinct tables (+0x0c of 0x013f57f8; +0x10 and +0x14 of 0x013fc06c; +0x14 and +0x60 of 0x01485550). A single named interface method cannot occupy four offsets, so this is a shared folded default body rather than one identifiable method, and no method name is claimed.

0x007f5403 carries an inlined duplicate of the identical body inside caller 0x007f53d0, two bytes after the JMP at 0x007f53fe that tail-transfers to it. A shipped header default the compiler can inline but sometimes emits out of line is the shape that produces both.

Every inspected consumer treats the answer as a byte predicate (TEST AL,AL), one of them compares it against the immediate 1 (CMP AL,0x1 at 0x00e81139), and two consumers discard it entirely. The only role the evidence supports is 'unconditional yes'.

The answer is a BYTE and the distinction is measurable: bits 8..31 of EAX are left as the caller left them. g++ compiling an ordinary C++ `return 1` here emits `mov eax,1` and writes all four bytes, so a restatement of this body is not byte-faithful under that compiler and the naked transcription is what makes it so.
unresolved_questions: What predicate is this? The body is a constant yes, but nothing in the observed evidence names the question it answers.
Which class or classes own the slots that point here? Four distinct slot offsets across three distinct tables are recorded above and they cannot all describe one method.

__fastcall is a SECOND surviving candidate in the derived record (conventions.candidate_conventions names both it and __thiscall) and nothing observed here closes it. The reconstruction asserts __thiscall because that is what the record's calling_convention field says, not because the second candidate was refuted.
Is the address a compiler-folded COMDAT shared by many unrelated 'return true' defaults, or a single default deliberately emitted once? Both fit every observation.
Is the always-true body a shipped default, a build-configuration stub, or a patch target at runtime? No differential trace has been captured for this function, so runtime patching cannot be excluded.
Why does caller 0x00a43050 and caller 0x0082c210 call the function and discard the answer? A constant with no side effects makes those calls no-ops in the observed build.

The Spore-ModAPI correspondence to IGameMode::func0Ch is a CANDIDATE for the 0x01485550 table only, recorded in sdk_correspondence and deliberately not asserted. Four offsets across three tables are why.

The 356 and 20 vtable-reference counts are raw pointer-scan totals, not proven distinct vtables. The true count is unmeasured. A scan of the image's own .rdata for the little-endian dword of this address finds 521 occurrences, and .data finds 17; those are also raw totals and are not a table count.

The six ECX receipt sites establish that a value is in ECX at the transfer. They do NOT establish that the body reads it, and the record's R2 says it does not. Whether the six sites pass the same object or six different ones is not determinable from the call sites alone.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace has been captured for 0x00b1fbf0, so every claim here is static. A runtime differential test must confirm that the answer is still 1 in the shipping build and that no runtime patch retargets the address.
The 0x00ee8860 virtual dispatch site must be observed with a concrete receiver before the slot's owning class can be named.
